newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down, Dow woes outweigh GDP.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down, Dow woes outweigh GDP.

text.p: Mexican stocks zigzagged in the opening minutes of trade on Monday to stand marginally lower as concern over the wavering Dow Jones counteracted strong GDP figures, dealers said.

"We have a lot of selling carried over from the tumble on Friday. GDP figures were marvellous, but are having little impact with everybody watching Wall Street and waiting for the Fed meeting tomorrow," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 4.12 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.08 percent, at 4,952.49.

The Finance Ministry announced minutes before trade opened that Mexico's GDP rose by 8.8 percent in the second quarter from year-ago figures. A previously conducted Reuters survey MEX22 of 13 Mexico City financial firms showed they had forecast an average rise of 5.92 percent.
Dealers noted that trading was cautious and volume very thin.
"There's hardly any shouting on the floor, it's very quiet here, and Telmex hasn't opened yet," a floor trader said, referring to Telfonos de Mxico, which has the heaviest weighting on the IPC index.
Volume was dead slow at 1.9 million shares, of which two cross trades accounted for one million.
Dealers said they were personally shaken by news of Saturday's killing of Alejandro Ortiz, brother of Finance Minister Ortiz, but did not foresee sharp market repercussions.
"It could slow investment flows a little, but will not lead to a sell-off," a desk trader said.
On the broad market, sliders outnumbered gainers by 10 to seven, out of a total of 25 stocks traded.
